name: salsa bruja
instructions:
A quart of pickled-chile 'witch's brine' — a hot vinegar-herb brine with boiled chiles poured over raw vegetables, sitting at room temperature until it's to your liking, then living in the fridge for months.

MAKES 1 QUART/LITER.

=== INGREDIENTS (BOOK VERSION — MY CHANGES IN NOTES) ===

THE BRINE:
- 1 1/2 cups apple cider vinegar (+ 1 1/2 cups water)
- 4 large chiles guajillos (1.4 oz/40g), stemmed and seeded (I used guajillo POWDER — fine; see notes)
- 24 fresh or dried chiles de árbol (0.8 oz/24g), stemmed — keep these WHOLE/REAL
- 4 1/2 tsp Diamond Crystal kosher salt (0.6 oz/18g)
- 3 dried bay leaves
- 2 fresh thyme sprigs
- 1 fresh rosemary sprig
- 1 tsp allspice berries
- 1 whole clove (I used powdered — fine; see notes)

THE VEGETABLES (RAW, IN THE JAR):
- 1/4 medium red onion (4 oz/112g), sliced
- 1 medium carrot (3.8 oz/110g), cut into sticks
- 2 celery stalks (3 oz/84g), ends trimmed, cut into sticks
- 2 chiles serranos (1.3 oz/38g), stemmed, sliced lengthwise into sticks (I used GREEN BELL PEPPER instead — see notes)
- 3 garlic cloves, peeled and smashed (but still holding their shape)

SPECIAL EQUIPMENT: 1-quart/liter NONREACTIVE container with a lid — glass, ceramic, stainless steel, food-grade plastic, or silicone.

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. THE BRINE: in a medium saucepan, combine 1 1/2 cups water, the vinegar, guajillos, chiles de árbol, salt, bay leaves, thyme, rosemary, allspice, and clove. Bring to a boil, cover, reduce to a simmer, cook 5 minutes. Remove from heat and let sit 10 minutes, until the chiles are very soft.
2. THE JAR: meanwhile, stuff the onion, carrot, celery, serranos (or bell pepper), and garlic into the 1-quart nonreactive container.
3. POUR the warm brine over the vegetables to cover. Seal and let sit at ROOM TEMPERATURE at least 3 hours and up to 3 days — flavors develop as it sits, so taste until it's to your liking.
4. REFRIGERATE for up to 6 MONTHS.
notes:
=== MY CHANGES (BOTH FINE) ===

- POWDERED CLOVES + POWDERED CHILES (EXCEPT THE ÁRBOL): I opted for powders over whole clove and whole guajillos, and it was fine. MIGHT BE BETTER with dried/real chiles — want to try the real thing.
- GREEN BELL PEPPER OVER SERRANO: the árbol chiles already add a lot of heat, so I swapped the serranos for green bell pepper in the jar. Also fine.

=== THE SHAPE OF THE RECIPE ===

Boiled-chile brine (the simmer softens and extracts the chiles) poured warm over raw vegetables — the vegetables pickle, the chiles carry. Room temp 3 hours to 3 days to develop, tasting as it goes; then fridge, up to 6 months.
